payload.problem_statement: High-speed railway embankments built on weak soil foundations experience long-term settlement that can exceed design tolerances, causing track geometry deviations and safety risks. Current practice relies on static pre-construction calculations (PLAXIS FEM) and periodic post-construction surveys — there is no continuous digital twin that ingests real-time instrumentation data, compares observed settlement against the approved design model, and alerts engineers when divergence exceeds safety thresholds in shadow mode alongside official calculations.
payload.observed_context: No existing GeoSophia codebase or artifacts found in the workspace. The saga-mcp repository contains D4 discovery-settlement engine files unrelated to geotechnical settlement. This is a greenfield product idea requiring domain research into geotechnical instrumentation standards, PLAXIS API capabilities, railway track geometry tolerances, and real-time monitoring systems used in dam/embankment engineering.
stakeholders_or_actors: Monitoring equipment vendors providing instrumentation data
assumptions: Instrumentation data is available at monitoring points during and after construction
Approved PLAXIS model parameters can be extracted or manually entered into the system
A simplified 1D consolidation model provides sufficient accuracy for early-warning divergence detection
Stakeholders accept a shadow-mode product that advises but does not replace regulatory calculations
Internet connectivity exists at construction sites, or edge devices can buffer and sync periodically
unknowns: Specific instrumentation standards and data formats used by Russian railway projects (RZD GOST vs international)
Whether PLAXIS models can be exported in machine-readable format preserving layer parameters
Regulatory requirements for settlement monitoring documentation in Russia (GOST R, SNiP) — whether shadow system outputs have recognized value
Typical data frequency from instrumentation (hourly, daily, event-triggered)
Existing commercial solutions and their feature/pricing expectations
Target deployment model: cloud SaaS, on-premise, or hybrid edge-cloud
risks: Technical: 1D consolidation models may produce false positives/negatives in complex geological conditions
Regulatory: Railway safety regulations may not recognize shadow-system outputs; liability for deviation from approved methods
Adoption: Geotechnical engineers are conservative; convincing them requires rigorous validation against known case studies
Data quality: Instrumentation failures produce gaps or outliers requiring graceful handling without false alerts
Integration: PLAXIS has limited API; manual parameter entry introduces transcription errors
payload.candidate_scope: Shadow-mode settlement risk monitoring service that: (1) ingests time-series data from embankment instrumentation via standard protocols, (2) maintains simplified 1D consolidation models calibrated to approved PLAXIS parameters per monitoring point, (3) computes real-time divergence with configurable alert thresholds, (4) produces risk dashboard with per-point status and PDF reports for regulatory review. Operates strictly in shadow mode with advisory-only outputs.
evidence_refs: Task description from Saga MCP task 6248: GeoSophia Settlement Twin objective
No existing codebase or artifacts found in workspace — greenfield product
Domain knowledge: Terzaghi 1D consolidation theory, PLAXIS industry-standard FEM software
payload.rationale: The idea addresses a genuine gap in railway embankment monitoring but requires clarification on four critical areas before formalization: (1) regulatory landscape for settlement monitoring documentation and advisory output recognition, (2) data availability from instrumentation feeds including formats and quality expectations, (3) PLAXIS integration path for model parameter ingestion, and (4) competitive landscape to differentiate the product. The core concept is sound but needs market validation and technical feasibility confirmation.
